vision.purpose:
A local-first pipeline of seven planning agents — CodeScanner, Brainstormer, Agentifier, Designer, StackAdvisor, Phaser, Deployer — that turns a rough idea or an existing codebase into a versioned folder of specs (`.spec4/v{N}/`), ready for a coding agent to execute phase by phase. Runs as a locally served web app at `localhost:8050`, with bring-your-own-key (BYOK) access across eight LLM providers; keys stay in the browser and never reach the server or disk.

This round's goal: rework the app's shell and home screen so Spec4 looks and behaves like a development tool rather than a marketing demo. The current UI shares a template with the marketing site (spec4.ai) — hero spacing, marketing-style agent cards, an external-link drawer, grid background, kicker labels, gradient text — which undermines credibility with its actual audience.
vision.ui_surface: Web app — Python, Dash, Dash Mantine Components — served locally at localhost:8050. Unchanged architecture; this round is a layout/density pass on existing components, not a rewrite.
target_audience: Developers who already use Claude Code, Kiro, or similar AI coding agents daily, and who are skeptical of spec-driven tooling. Single audience — no secondary users.

Development Tool Shell.description: Header becomes a status bar: working directory (monospace), round (v{N}), default provider and model (monospace), Spec4 version. Primary nav: Project, Artifacts, Settings, plus one Docs link. Removes the external-link drawer, footer, and in-app landing page. Removes grid background, kicker labels, gradient text, hero spacing, card hover effects, button glows, and all emoji. Cuts vertical spacing roughly in half. Keeps the dark theme. #39FF14 green becomes the sole Mantine primary/accent color (primary buttons, active state, focus rings); secondary buttons are neutral outlines. #1E88E5 blue survives only in the wordmark. Monospace for any file, path, command, model name, or figure.
Development Tool Shell.example: The header reads as a status line, not a hero banner.

Open To The Project.description: When a working directory is remembered, `/` opens the project view directly; otherwise it opens the directory picker. No introduction screen.
Open To The Project.example: Returning users land straight in their project, not on a splash page.

Round Tree.description: The project view's first element is the current round's `.spec4/v{N}/` folder as a tree: one line per artifact in pipeline order, each with a status — present, needs update (an upstream artifact is newer), or missing. Files are colored by lane with a three-item legend: prompts for the agent (phases/), reference for the agent (code_review.json, vision.json, feature_specs.json, ai_features.json, design/mock.html, design/manifest.json, stack.json), a record for you (deployment-plan.md, usage.json). Status comes from the existing dependency graph; usage.json is never marked needs-update. Display only this round — opening a file is the next round.
Round Tree.example: The round is shown as its files.

Agent Rows.description: The seven agents as compact rows in pipeline order replace the cards. Each row: agent name, the artifact it produces (monospace), the model it last ran on this round (from usage.json's per-agent models list; blank if it has not run), tokens in and out this round, and the action button using the existing state model — Start, Modify, Needs Update, Not Ready, Required — with its existing semantics and routing. No step numbers, descriptions, or emoji.
Agent Rows.example: A dense list of agent status rows, not a grid of descriptive cards.

Round Cost.description: The round's estimated cost so far, from usage.json totals, on the project view, following the cost card's existing labelling rules: labelled 'estimated', tokens shown, calls that could not be priced named and excluded, never '$0.0000' for unknown.
Round Cost.example: "Estimated cost, v0: $0.7312 · 2 of 19 calls could not be priced and are excluded" — never "$0.0000".

differentiators: The open `.spec4` file format — existing, unchanged; this round makes it visible for the first time by showing the round as its files (the round tree).
Any LLM model usable at any pipeline step — existing, unchanged.

Chat Frame Register (v1).description: The chat frame — agent pill bar, transcript, action row, cost card, model chip, status line — keeps every function and adopts the same register: denser framing, green primary buttons, no emoji, monospace for counters and model names.

Artifact View (v1).description: An artifact view that renders any .spec4 file in monospace, reached from the round tree and from an Open button beside each Download button.

Register Extension (v2).description: The setup wizard, per-agent gate card, project-mode question, directory picker, and Designer wizard inherit the dev-tool register established in this round.

constraints: Dash and Dash Mantine Components remain the UI foundation — this round is a layout and density pass on existing components, not a rewrite.
API keys never reach the server or disk.
The gate card, model chip, and retry panel share one model-selection path; nothing parallel is added.
Existing component ids are a test contract and are kept.
usage.json stays out of the dependency graph (never contributes to staleness/status).
Standing rule for every element on screen: if it is not a fact, a command, an artifact, or a control, it goes.
